note: Microsoft Fabric IQ facts with dated sources. Ontology, its agent integrations and operations agents are in preview: re-check the sources and Fabric known issues before a workshop (90-day rule). The overall checked date and S1-S44 are historical; G59 citations and current_guidance record the 17 November 2026 governance/SAP correction. Use the Common Data Model in silver, medallion layers in OneLake, gold semantic models, the Cloud Adoption Framework data product standard and current OneLake catalog/Fabric domain grouping guidance.

governance.text: For new designs use OneLake catalog for discovery and source-qualified governance, and Fabric domains for grouping associated workspaces and items. Fabric domain assignment does not change visibility or access and is not an ACL or security boundary. Unified Catalog and classic Purview data governance are retiring: no new accounts, maintenance through 12 November 2027. Preserve existing Purview-estate context and Purview security/compliance, sensitivity labels and DLP, alongside workspace/item permissions and OneLake security. Confirm contractual, regulated and feature gaps with the governance owner and account team; no full feature parity is claimed.

sap.text: The documented candidate for supported SAP families is SAP Datasphere -> ADLS Gen2 -> Fabric/OneLake: an initial snapshot and changes are merged into OneLake Delta tables with a read-only SQL replica. Confirm source support, existing Fabric capacity, a suitable SAP Datasphere Premium Outbound Integration environment, entitlement, ADLS Gen2 staging and required permissions with the named source owner. SAP Datasphere Premium Outbound Integration: unpriced / to confirm. A source-name or public-document match proves none of these estate prerequisites. Unknown routes stay unresolved, not an automatically selected pipeline. Even an owner-asserted design choice is not tenant verification, licence readiness, provider GA or publication authority.

stack.name: OneLake
stack.what: One governed data lake for the organisation: systems of record arrive through mirroring and shortcuts, without building copy pipelines where an open format allows it; OneLake catalog, OneLake security and sensitivity labels govern access.

stack.name: Power BI semantic models
stack.what: The curated analytics layer with measures and hierarchies; an ontology can be generated from a semantic model and carries its DAX measures as metrics.

stack.name: Ontology (preview)
stack.what: The business context layer of Fabric IQ: entity types, properties, relationships, rules and metrics, bound to live data in OneLake so people, applications and agents share one vocabulary.

stack.name: Agents grounded in the ontology
stack.what: The ontology agent, Fabric data agents (questions and answers), operations agents (monitoring and actions with approval in Teams), Copilot Studio agents (Fabric IQ MCP tool), Foundry IQ agents and custom agents through the ontology MCP server.

unresolved.what: No route has been selected. Ask the source owner to confirm support, environment, entitlement and permissions.

mirroring.what: Mirroring adds a supported external database or catalog and keeps it in sync in OneLake. SAP is conditional: the source-qualified Datasphere -> ADLS Gen2 -> Fabric/OneLake route needs owner-confirmed prerequisites; a system name selects no route.

shortcut.what: A shortcut references tables or folders in an open format (Delta, Iceberg) where they live, for example in Azure Data Lake Storage, Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage or Dataverse.

eventstream.what: Live events and telemetry stream into an eventhouse (Real-Time Intelligence) and bind as time series.

pipeline.what: A pipeline or copy job loads sources that neither mirroring nor shortcuts cover; curated tables land in a lakehouse or warehouse.

semantic model.what: An existing Power BI semantic model is reused: generate the ontology from it, or bind to it (check the known issue for agents).

supported_source.note: Confirm the source family with its data owner.

datasphere_environment.note: Confirm a suitable SAP Datasphere environment.

adls_gen2_permissions.note: Confirm ADLS Gen2 staging and required permissions.

sap_route_assessment.commercial_note: SAP Datasphere Premium Outbound Integration: unpriced / to confirm.

m365_copilot.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
m365_copilot.how: Publish the data agent to the Agent Store; users chat with it or @mention it in Copilot and Teams.

copilot_studio.name: Copilot Studio
copilot_studio.how: Add the data agent to a Copilot Studio agent, or ground the agent in the ontology with the Fabric IQ MCP tool (list_ontology_entity_types, search_ontology).

foundry.name: Microsoft Foundry
foundry.how: Use the ontology as a Fabric IQ knowledge source in a Foundry IQ knowledge base.

teams.name: Microsoft Teams
teams.how: Operations agents send recommendations to the Fabric Operations Agent Teams app; a person approves or rejects each action.

build_steps.name: Unify and conform the data in OneLake
build_steps.what: Bring systems of record into bronze through a source-qualified route, then conform business entities to the Common Data Model in silver and curate gold data products. SAP stays conditional until the named owner confirms support, existing Fabric capacity, Datasphere Premium Outbound Integration and ADLS Gen2 permissions; its snapshot/changes become OneLake Delta tables with a read-only SQL replica. The SAP commercial dependency is unpriced / to confirm. The ontology binds to managed silver tables without column mapping, with string/integer keys and UTC timestamps for time series.

build_steps.name: Create the ontology
build_steps.what: Create an empty ontology (preview) item and import ontology.ttl (owl:Class becomes an entity type, owl:DatatypeProperty a property, owl:ObjectProperty a relationship type; labels, descriptions and synonyms are kept). Or generate it from an existing semantic model.

build_steps.name: Bind the data
build_steps.what: Bind every entity type to its OneLake source and choose its key; bind relationship types and time series. The ontology agent proposes bindings in Plan mode; a person applies them in Act mode.

build_steps.name: Add rules and metrics
build_steps.what: Add the business rules in natural language and the metrics from the DAX measures of the journey's gold semantic model; create a named version.

build_steps.name: Data agents
build_steps.what: Create one Fabric data agent per journey with the ontology as its context source (up to five sources per agent), add instructions and example queries, test, then publish to Microsoft 365 Copilot or add it to the Copilot Studio agents of the journey.

build_steps.name: Operations agents
build_steps.what: Create an operations agent per monitored process with the ontology as knowledge, natural-language rules and actions; recommendations arrive in Teams for approval.

build_steps.name: Govern
build_steps.what: Workspace and item permissions, OneLake security, Purview sensitivity labels and DLP protect the bound data; agents answer with the user's permissions. Use OneLake catalog for discovery and source-qualified governance, with Fabric domains as logical grouping, never access grants. Confirm owner, purpose, uses, access, quality and upstream source routes before publication. Keep existing Purview-estate transition gaps with the governance owner and account team; no full parity claim.

readiness.item: Fabric capacity F2 or higher (or Power BI Premium P1 with Fabric enabled) in the region of the data; trial capacities don't run operations agents
readiness.why: Data agents and operations agents need a paid capacity

readiness.item: Tenant settings: users can create ontology (preview) items and Fabric items
readiness.why: Prerequisite to create and import the ontology

readiness.item: Tenant settings for data agents: Copilot and Azure OpenAI; cross-geo processing and storing for AI where the capacity is outside the US and EU
readiness.why: Data agents and operations agents use Azure OpenAI
readiness.owner: Fabric administrator with the data protection officer

readiness.item: Operations agent settings and the Fabric Operations Agent Teams app for the approvers
readiness.why: Recommendations and approvals arrive in Teams

readiness.item: Workspaces and Fabric domain grouping for the process ontology (DEV, TEST, PROD), with owners per namespace; domain assignment does not grant visibility or access
readiness.why: Ownership, lifecycle and CI/CD; access controls remain separate from grouping

readiness.item: Source-qualified OneLake routes with named owners and service identities; SAP remains conditional until support, existing Fabric capacity, Datasphere Premium Outbound Integration environment/entitlement and ADLS Gen2 permissions are confirmed
readiness.why: Recorded routes or done verdicts do not resolve missing SAP prerequisites; the commercial dependency remains unpriced / to confirm
readiness.owner: Data platform owner with the system owners

readiness.item: Binding-ready tables: managed lakehouse tables without column mapping, string or integer keys, time series with a UTC timestamp
readiness.why: Data binding limitations of the preview

readiness.item: Copilot Studio production environment with the ontology MCP tools allowed (Fabric IQ MCP)
readiness.why: Copilot Studio agents grounded in the ontology

readiness.item: Copilot extensibility enabled to publish data agents to the Agent Store in Microsoft 365 Copilot
readiness.why: Business users reach the data agents in Copilot and Teams

readiness.item: OneLake security roles, sensitivity labels and DLP policies on the bound items
readiness.why: Agents answer with the user's permissions; labels and DLP protect exports

readiness.item: Medallion lakehouses per domain: bronze (mirroring, shortcuts, eventstreams), silver tables conformed to the Common Data Model, gold data products; materialized lake views where no copy is needed
readiness.why: The ontology binds to conformed, binding-ready tables; the data products build on them

readiness.item: Link to Fabric for Dataverse and Dynamics 365 (workspace identity), with the tables the ontology needs, finance and operations tables included
readiness.why: Brings the Common Data Model tables into OneLake without copy pipelines

readiness.item: Data product standard per domain: accountable owner, business purpose, intended uses, access process, quality status; endorsement meanings (promoted, certified); sensitivity labels
readiness.why: The minimum to publish a data product that agents may use
readiness.owner: Chief data officer with the domain owners

readiness.item: OneLake catalog discovery and source-qualified governance, with Fabric domain grouping for shared business objects and journeys; retain existing Purview-estate transition context, sensitivity labels and DLP
readiness.why: Grouping is not access; assess contractual, regulated and feature gaps with the governance owner and account team, without a parity claim

readiness.item: A gold semantic model per journey in Direct Lake on OneLake (star schema) that owns the measures behind the ontology's metrics
readiness.why: Metrics with one definition for reports, the ontology and the agents

risks.title: Ontology, its agent integrations and operations agents are in preview and can change
risks.mitigation: Keep the ontology definition in ontology.ttl and the repository; re-check the Microsoft Learn sources and the Fabric known issues before each phase; the old ontology experience retires on 31 January 2027

risks.title: Data agents and operations agents don't work with an ontology bound to semantic models (known issue)
risks.mitigation: Bind the entity types that agents use to lakehouse, warehouse or eventhouse tables; reuse semantic-model measures as metrics; re-check the known issue

risks.title: Keys and master data are not clean enough to relate the entity instances across systems
risks.mitigation: Profile the key columns before binding; agree one key per entity type with its data owner; map cross-system keys in the curated layer

risks.title: Answers of data agents published to Microsoft 365 Copilot can leave Fabric's compliance boundary or region
risks.mitigation: Review with the data protection officer before publishing to the Agent Store; keep sensitive data agents inside Fabric or Copilot Studio

risks.title: Capacity consumption of data agents, graph queries and operations agents is not yet known
risks.mitigation: Measure consumption in the prototype on a dedicated capacity; add it to the FinOps model before scaling

risks.title: Source data doesn't map cleanly to the Common Data Model (SAP or custom fields), so the silver layer needs mapping work and custom extensions
risks.mitigation: Map the MVP entity types first and verify columns with the table definition browser. Keep SAP route support, capacity, Datasphere Premium Outbound Integration and ADLS Gen2 permissions as separate owner-confirmation gaps; mapping is not route or entitlement proof.

risks.title: A data product approved for analytics or AI grounding is reused by an agent that takes actions, without a new review
risks.mitigation: List intended uses and upstream conditional route gaps per product; review agent actions and external sharing separately. Fabric domain grouping is not access permission; keep security controls and existing governance transition gaps explicit.

decisions.question: One enterprise ontology with a namespace per journey, or one ontology per domain?
decisions.recommendation: One ontology with namespaces while the journeys share core entity types (Customer, Product, Asset); split when ownership or lifecycle differ
decisions.owner: Enterprise architecture with the data owners

decisions.question: Bind to Power BI semantic models or to lakehouse and warehouse tables?
decisions.recommendation: Generate from semantic models to reuse definitions and measures; bind the entity types that agents use to tables until the known issue is resolved

decisions.question: Which systems of record are mirrored, which are shortcuts and which need a pipeline?
decisions.recommendation: Use source-qualified routes. SAP is unresolved until its owner confirms support, existing Fabric capacity, Datasphere Premium Outbound Integration and ADLS Gen2 permissions. The documented candidate is read-only replication via Datasphere and ADLS Gen2, not direct mirroring from any SAP estate or an automatic pipeline fallback; its commercial dependency is unpriced / to confirm.
decisions.owner: Data platform owner with the system owners

decisions.question: Which data agents are published to Microsoft 365 Copilot, and which serve only the journey's Copilot Studio agents?
decisions.recommendation: Start inside Fabric and Copilot Studio; publish to the Agent Store after the data protection review
decisions.owner: Journey owner with the data protection officer

decisions.question: Which canonical model do the silver tables follow: the Common Data Model, or the source systems' own models?
decisions.recommendation: The Common Data Model entities and Dataverse column names, with custom extensions only where no standard entity exists; Dynamics 365 data arrives in that shape through Link to Fabric
decisions.owner: Enterprise architecture with the data platform owner

decisions.question: Who owns each data product, what is its quality commitment, and which uses need an additional review?
decisions.recommendation: The journey's business owner owns its data products; agent actions and external sharing always need a review; promote first, certify after the first release
decisions.owner: Chief data officer with the domain owners

data_architecture.principle: Each entity type of the ontology rests on a Microsoft standard entity where one exists: a Common Data Model entity (the Dataverse tables of Dynamics 365 and Power Platform), a Dataverse table of a Dynamics 365 app, or a finance and operations table published in the Common Data Model. Silver tables are conformed to those entities and columns, so every system of record lands in one shared shape; custom extensions only where no standard entity exists.

layers.name: Bronze
layers.what: Raw data as it arrives, in the shape of the source: mirrored databases, shortcuts (Link to Fabric for Dataverse and Dynamics 365), eventstreams into an eventhouse, pipelines. No changes are made here.

layers.name: Silver
layers.what: Business entities conformed to the Common Data Model: errors fixed, formats standardised, duplicates removed, records matched across systems. One Delta table per entity type in the domain's silver lakehouse; materialized lake views over shortcuts where no copy is needed; live events in the eventhouse. The ontology binds here.

layers.name: Gold
layers.what: Data products: curated tables and star schemas (facts and dimensions) per journey, served by Power BI semantic models in Direct Lake mode, the ideal storage mode for the gold layer. The semantic models own the DAX measures behind the ontology's metrics.

layers.name: Ontology (Fabric IQ)
layers.what: The business vocabulary over silver and gold: entity types, relationships, rules and metrics that data agents, operations agents, Copilot Studio and Foundry agents use.

data_architecture.intake: Prefer source-qualified shortcuts or mirroring when supported, data movement only when required. SAP needs owner confirmation of the Datasphere -> ADLS Gen2 -> Fabric/OneLake prerequisites and unpriced commercial dependency; no route is selected from its name. Make source data available only for an approved analytical need.

domains.fabric: Group associated workspaces/items in Fabric domains for journeys and shared business objects, with named owners. Assignment does not change visibility or access; configure permissions and OneLake security separately.
domains.purview_what: Use current OneLake catalog guidance for new discovery/governance proposals. Retain existing Purview-estate context, labels and DLP; resolve regulated, contractual and feature transition gaps with the account team. No full parity is claimed.

data_architecture.semantic_models: One semantic model per journey on its gold lakehouse in Direct Lake on OneLake: fact tables for the journey's events and transactions, conformed dimensions for the shared business objects and a date table; the measures behind the ontology's metrics. Bind the ontology's entity types to lakehouse tables, not to the semantic model, while data agents and operations agents don't support semantic-model bindings (R-ONT-2).

data_product_standard.what: A data product is one or more technical assets that together provide a supported business offering; the owning domain is accountable for it.
data_product_standard.publication_note: Every published data product needs an accountable owner, a supported business purpose, intended use, an access process and a quality status; an operational commitment when consumers depend on timely availability; security controls and sensitivity labels before publication; lineage to judge upstream dependencies and downstream impact.

endorsement.promoted: The owning domain recommends the data product for reuse
endorsement.certified: An authorized reviewer confirmed that the data product meets the organisation's standards

data_product_standard.consumption: The owning domain defines the uses each data product supports. Approval for one use doesn't imply approval for another: a data product approved for AI grounding isn't automatically approved for an agent that can take consequential actions, and internal reporting doesn't imply external publication.
data_product_standard.discovery: OneLake catalog for discovery, endorsement and source-qualified governance; Fabric domains group workspaces/items without granting access. Preserve existing Purview-estate transition context; confirm feature, contractual and regulated gaps with the account team, without a full-parity claim.
data_product_standard.security: A consumption path must not weaken the protection the data product needs: Fabric data agents and Power BI keep the user's identity; indexes and service identities need their own authorization boundary.
